lines.text: Pearls often start as Mississippi mussel shell.
lines.say: Pearls often start as miss-ih-SIP-ee mussel shell.

lines.text: A cultured pearl grows around a round bead called a nucleus.
The beads are polished spheres of freshwater mussel shell.
Most of the shell comes from the Mississippi and Tennessee river systems.
lines.say: Most of the shell comes from the miss-ih-SIP-ee and Tennessee river systems.

lines.text: Makers saw shell into strips, then grind cubes into spheres.
One shell yields about 20 beads, a few percent of its weight.
lines.say: One shell yields about twenty beads, a few percent of its weight.

lines.text: Most beads measure 6 to 8 millimeters across.
lines.say: Most beads measure six to eight millimeters across.

lines.text: A tiny piece of mantle tissue goes in beside the bead.
Coating it with nacre usually takes one to a few years.
lines.say: Coating it with NAY-ker usually takes one to a few years.

lines.text: By the 1950s, shell from American rivers was shipping to Japan.
lines.say: By the nineteen fifties, shell from American rivers was shipping to Japan.
